text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- More new firms and fewer insolvencies are expected in 1997. However credit protection agency KSV expects difficult times for medium-sized companies.
- New Social Democrat party manager Andreas Rudas wants to change a lot in the party as well as create jobs and work with the media.
- Union boss Lorenz Fritz wants the billions of schillings freed up by the government to promote new technology to be used for an export offensive.
- Austria celebrates its first medal in the skiing world championships in Italy's Sestriere. Guenther Mader won the bronze medal in the men's Super-G race.
- Only big retail chains have so far profited from longer shopping hours introduced at the beginning of the year.
- Austria's tourism industry is bringing in a new reservation system and the national tourism board is planning a major advertising offensive to coincide with its introduction.
- Austria's tourism income went down in 1996 but good winter sales could slow the fall slightly.
- German baker Mueller shows interest in taking over Austria's Ankerbrot because the latter's owner Helmut Schuster is thinking about quitting.

- Industry union boss Lorenz Fritz praised Austria's new Chancellor Viktor Klima while criticising social partners labour unions and trade unions. He wants exports to be improved and demands more flexible working hours.

- Lower Austria, Upper Austria and Styria have created a common concept on the participation of regional government in federal grid company Verbund. However, the Social Democrats have shown a reluctance to agree to the plan.
